editorial.headline: When an Open Wholesale Trade Meets Bali’s PMA Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale activity is open to full foreign ownership nationally, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks registration there today.
editorial.body:
KBLI 46209 covers wholesale trade in other agricultural products and live animals not classified elsewhere. Its stated terrain includes agricultural residues and waste, agricultural by-products used for animal feed, and other plants and plant seedlings. It is a deliberately broad wholesale category: the common thread is the trading of these agricultural goods, rather than a single named commodity.

The activity is open across the full scale range recorded for it: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the category is not confined to one business size. A wholesale operator working with the agricultural materials, feed-related by-products, plants, seedlings, or live animals within this scope can place the activity at any of those listed scales.

Nationally, the position is straightforward. The PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. A 100% national ceiling does not overcome Bali’s block on PMA registration.

Bali reaches a different conclusion. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO: a PMA applicant cannot register this activity in Bali today. The record says that, at the Besar scale, every scope carries an OSS risk classification of Rendah or Menengah-Rendah, placing it within Bali’s moratorium noted as May 13, 2026. That provincial rule blocks PMA registration island-wide and permanently for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. This is not a reduction of the national foreign-ownership ceiling; it is a Bali-specific bar on PMA registration for the activity.
